perspective:
Keith’s available information:

- He works as a construction worker at a construction company; Elizabeth is the receptionist and a colleague. They have a friendly but professional relationship, mainly through his office visits for paperwork and project updates.
- Recently, he noticed Elizabeth had been unusually curt with him over several days. He wondered if he had upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- He asked Elizabeth if he had done something to upset her. He heard her say no, not at all; she was dealing with personal stuff and was sorry if she seemed short.
- He told her he understood she was going through a tough time, offered to listen, and suggested a coffee break. He heard her accept and thank him.
- Over coffee, Elizabeth shared more about her stresses; Keith perceived them as quite severe. He thanked her for sharing, asked if she had considered talking to a professional, and mentioned an external perspective can help. He heard her say she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, he observed Elizabeth become slightly withdrawn. He believed his suggestion might have embarrassed her and felt regretful. He told her he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her no matter what. He heard her say he didn’t overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was a lot to think about.
- Later, he observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative of his concern. He believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him. He told her he was glad they talked and that he was always there if she needed to chat or take a break. He heard her thank him, say it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- He intends to maintain this supportive relationship.
